_note: Lane decided the pairs and strengths on 2026-11-12 (Lev 26 / Deut 28). The 17 verse pairs T01-T17 mirror Deuteronomy/data/mirror-leviticus.json, here and other swapped; LD0 is the frame. Spans are English numbering. strength: 3 shared words, 2 same story beat, 1 thematic.

sources.cite: Jeffrey H. Tigay, Deuteronomy, JPS Torah Commentary (Philadelphia: Jewish Publication Society, 1996), Excursus 26, pp. 489–92 (structure of Deut 28), with a cross-reference of Lev 26:19 to Deut 28:23.
sources.what: Pointer: Tigay calls both chapters a 'tokhehah', divides Deut 28 into blessings (1–14) and curses (15–68), and notes the matched six blessings and curses.
sources.boundary_note: Lev 26 is touched in passing there. Pairs and shared words come from the verses.

sources.cite: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (morphhb: Westminster Leningrad Codex with Strong's-based lemmas), https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb, pinned morphhb@2.0.2; English verse numbers via its VerseMap.xml.
sources.what: Every Strong's number in a `shared` entry was found in both cited verses by script.
sources.boundary_note: Lemma overlap shows shared vocabulary, not shared meaning; a shared word can be used in a different sense in each place.

pairs.title: Blessings, then curses: the same shape in two chapters
pairs.strength_why: Same beat across the whole: if you keep the commands, blessings; if you do not, curses in escalating stages.
pairs.note: Lev 26 sets the curses in stages marked 'seven times' (vv. 18, 21, 24, 28); Deut 28 has a longer curse half (15–68) and a hinge at v. 45. Wide pair: the narrower pairs below nest inside it.

pairs.title: If you keep the commandments, blessings
pairs.strength_why: Both open the blessings with keeping and doing the commandments.

pairs.title: Rain in its season
pairs.strength_why: Same promise (rain given in its season); the word for rain differs, so only 'give' and 'season' are shared.

pairs.title: Enemies fall before you
pairs.strength_why: Same beat: enemies are beaten before Israel; the verbs differ (struck vs fall by the sword).

pairs.title: The LORD establishes you
pairs.strength_why: Same beat: God confirms Israel (a holy people / his covenant); one shared verb, 'establish'.

pairs.title: The yoke: broken, then iron
pairs.strength_why: Both name a yoke; Lev says God broke its bars, Deut says he puts an iron one on.

pairs.title: Egypt and slavery reversed
pairs.strength_why: Lev 26:13 brought you out of Egypt so you would not be slaves; Deut 28:68 sends you back to be sold as slaves.

pairs.title: But if you will not listen
pairs.strength_why: Both open the curses with not listening and not doing the commandments and statutes.

pairs.title: Consumption and fever
pairs.strength_why: The same two disease words appear in both lists.

pairs.title: Seed sown, others consume it
pairs.strength_why: Same beat (sown seed lost); only 'seed' is shared and the eater differs (locust vs enemies).

pairs.title: Struck before your enemies, you flee
pairs.strength_why: Near word for word: struck before the enemy, and flee (Deut: seven ways; Lev: with none pursuing).

pairs.title: Sky and earth as metal
pairs.strength_why: Same image; the metals are swapped (Lev sky iron, soil bronze; Deut sky bronze, earth iron).
pairs.note: Tigay points to an Assyrian parallel to this image (figures-tigay item 20); not used here.

pairs.title: Pestilence
pairs.strength_why: The same word for pestilence; in Lev it comes with the covenant sword, in Deut it clings until Israel is consumed.

pairs.title: Eating the flesh of sons and daughters
pairs.strength_why: Same four words: eat, flesh, sons, daughters. Deut adds the siege and the detail of 28:54–57.

pairs.title: Scattered among the nations
pairs.strength_why: Same beat (scattering); Deut says 'peoples', Lev 'nations' (the shared word, 'nations', turns up in Deut 28:65).
pairs.note: Only 'land' is shared inside these two verses, so no shared entry.

pairs.title: A fearful heart among the enemy
pairs.strength_why: Same beat: terror of heart in exile; Lev adds flight at a leaf's sound, Deut adds no rest and day-and-night dread. Could be a 3 on the shared 'heart'.

pairs.title: Animals
pairs.strength_why: Thematic only: in Lev wild animals rob you of children; in Deut animals eat the corpses.

pairs.title: Astonishment
pairs.strength_why: Thematic only: in Lev your enemies are astonished at the land; in Deut Israel becomes an astonishment among the peoples.
